name: psu-v1-stepped
description: Modified psu-v1: sustained phase replaced with isolated CPU step-up then GPU step-up (20% increments, 30s each). Phases 3+ unchanged from psu-v1. Tests PSU regulation under single-rail ramp, exposes step-response droop and transient compensation before hitting the full-sustained stress pattern.

phases.name: baseline
phases.notes: 15s idle baseline. Capture reference rail voltages and temps for drift rules.

phases.name: cpu-step-20
phases.notes: CPU at 20% — first rail-step. Watch 12V droop response.

phases.name: cpu-step-100
phases.notes: CPU at 100% — sustained ceiling on CPU-only rails.

phases.name: cpu-gpu-settle
phases.notes: 5s all-idle. Lets CPU rails recover and settle before GPU ramp. Captures the step-down transient.

phases.name: gpu-step-20
phases.notes: GPU at 20% TDP (nvidia-smi -pl). First GPU-rail step.

phases.name: gpu-step-100
phases.notes: GPU at 100% TDP — sustained ceiling on GPU-only rails.

phases.name: rail-swap
phases.notes: 5 min out-of-phase — CPU loaded while GPU idles, then swap every 5s. Forces the PSU to rapidly shift which 12V rail group carries the load. Multi-rail PSUs are especially vulnerable to regulation crossover.

phases.name: gpu-only
phases.notes: 5 min GPU maxed, CPU idle. Asymmetric 12V loading — exposes weak regulation on GPU-side rails.

phases.name: cpu-only
phases.notes: 5 min CPU maxed, GPU idle. Opposite asymmetry — sudden ~550W drop on GPU rails, full load on CPU rails.

phases.name: transient
phases.notes: 5 min GPU pinned, CPU 1s on/off. ~350W transient at near-max load. One phase is enough — caps and feedback loops either handle it or they don't.
